title: Finite compatibility of the explicitly composed chart pairs
statement: Fix the field, prime, coefficient and calculus data of the coordinate theorem and foundations a [lem-sp-coordinate-foundations], together with projection adjunctions p [lem-sp-coordinate-projection-models]. Define coordinateChartPair by composing the calculus etale sum-extension pair with p.projection, transporting the left side by the etale-shriek and compact-support composition isomorphisms, and the right side by a.pulled and composeRight [lem-sp-coordinate-restricted-composition]. For every separated finite-type etale k-chart e:U→A^d_Y and every chart compactification, this explicit pair admits LevelCompatibility on all finite constructible finite-Tor objects, with left comparison supportEvaluation and right comparison rightEvaluation [def-sp-coordinate-right-comparisons]. Its ambient counit is the displayed composite: inverse pulled right comparison, inverse compact-support composition, compact support of the etale-shriek comparison and fibre sum, followed by p.projection counit, for every intermediate compactification. This asserts compatibility of an already constructed adjunction, not existence of a new chart adjunction.

source.place: Local pairs and Levels; explicit categorical details of the original coordinate argument

proof.text: First construct coordinateChartPair using restrictedComposite. Its left closure is Preservation and its right closure is foundation chart_closed. For the coefficient-independent intermediate compactifications chosen before deriving, apply restrictedComposite_counit and expand the inverse of the composite left comparison. This proves coordinateChartPair_counit with etale fibre summation preceding integration. For any other intermediate compactifications, use the calculus refinement naturality and composition coherence to identify the same counit; naturality of the projection counit gives the stated formula. At each finite level compose the finite etale pair with the projection finite pair, on all finite constructible finite-Tor objects. Evaluate the actual tower constructions via supportEvaluation and rightEvaluation. The constituent etale and projection transpose equations imply both composite transpose equations. Apply them to identities to obtain unit and counit compatibility. No faithfulness of derived evaluation is used.
